purpose: E.V. v4's machine-readable spec: collections, tasks, environments, capacity, boundaries and working agreements. Pipelines, build chats and the page read this instead of prose; the design is the E.V. Foundation v4 doc.

_rules: Every pipeline follows the run protocol (core/run.mjs): start, pull, compute, apply, end; each move prints the exact calls.

A step is code (core/steps.mjs CODE_STEPS), or agent: a named judgment, the material it is shown, the shape of its answer and the fold that turns the answer into writes. Code does every step with one right answer.
reads is the pull: the collections a run reads, with windowDays where only recent documents matter. The journal is in no read set (D-059).
steps null means the pipeline's steps arrive with the backlog task in pendingIn; its task is not created before then.

B-172: 'failed' is what Matt reads when a run fails, in plain words and never led by 'E.V.' (a push cut at the first sentence end showed only 'E.V.' on Oct 21). Every failure line is '<failed> (<pipeline>): <the reason>. A build chat will look.', rendered by core/run.mjs failLine for the end move and by the prompt for a failure before the code runs.

morning.purpose: builds today's practice (the review set and any drill the exam plan calls for) and the day's plan and list before the 5am alarm
morning.failed: Today's practice and plan weren't built

reads.why: D-111: the push line names a stale health check; no Derived document reads it

steps.does: plans the day, picks the weak spots due for review, the new checks and the drills the plan calls for, and finds the passages in his materials each one rests on

steps.judgment: Write today's review and drill questions from the brief: one review item per target weak spot (from a new angle if it has history), one check per objective listed, and each drill's count of items on its chapters and objectives. Ground every item in the passages given; match their terms and values. Each item: type single|sata|matrix (numeric only in a numeric drill), stem (10+ characters), options (2 to 6) and correct (indexes) or a matrix, rationales, objective, topic, cjStep (one of the six clinical-judgment steps), sourceRef (materials/<id> it rests on) or verify: true when the point is not in his materials; a review item names its weakspotId target; never select-N; only exam content, never graded work. A drill marked numeric is a dosage drill (D-100): only type numeric items, each with stem (the order, what is on hand, and the rounding asked for), answer (a number), unit (one of spec.items.units), tolerance (half the rounding step: 0.05 for tenths, 0.5 for whole drops; 0 when exact), steps (the worked solution, one line each), objective, topic, cjStep and sourceRef (one of that drill's passages); work the numbers from the passages' methods; never from his medication table or drug cards.

steps.does: the day before a NUR unit exam, writes predictions/<examId>: readiness as of this morning, which calibrate reads with the score Matt enters (D-094)
builds days/<date>: the plan, the list and the push line

evening-cloud.purpose: parks weak spots whose exam has passed, recomputes every weak spot from his answers and writes the snapshot the page and lint check against

steps.does: parks the weak spots of exams that have passed (an event each)
writes state/current: the snapshot (with tomorrow's prep check when tomorrow is a clinical, lab, validation or class day, built from its materials, B-107), the derived hash and every Fact's hash

composes the push line from state/current and tomorrow's day: tomorrow's pack check when tomorrow is a prep day (B-107), review answered or left, weak spots made solid or reopened today, tomorrow's day type and first item, last night's Canvas note (B-40); never from the journal

weekly.purpose: writes his Sunday review of the week from the week's answers, weak spots, sessions and runs

steps.does: rolls up the week: answers by objective and type, weak spots added and made solid, study minutes, runs, calibration

steps.judgment: Check, read-only, that this record runs the build it should: make each listed read exactly as listed, in order, and save each result as its note says, with the printed tool-result command, never retyped. When list_triggers returns a next_cursor, call it again with the same arguments plus that cursor and save the next page the same way, until there is none. Change nothing. Answer saved: true when every read was made and saved; if a read is refused, stop there and answer saved: false with the refusal quoted.

Write the week's review for Matt from the brief: what moved, what is still weak (nearest exam first), the coming week's dates, any failed runs, one suggestion for next week; then one reflection question for him to write about, and a one-line push. The brief's insights are the week's numbers, computed by code (B-72): say in a sentence or two what they mean for next week (the weakest objective, an item missed every time, what keeps coming back, how study minutes sat against the next day's accuracy); quote them, never recompute or round them differently. Plain, warm, under 3000 characters. Never about graded work.

evening-mac.purpose: brings in Canvas changes read-only through his signed-in browser tab, and saves the nightly backup (and on Sundays the Markdown mirror) to his Mac
evening-mac.failed: Tonight's Canvas check and backup didn't run

input.mirror: yes: write the Markdown mirror tonight even though it isn't Sunday

steps.judgment: Bring Canvas in, read-only, as the material says: find the Canvas tab in the built-in browser (open one if there is none); if it shows a sign-in page, stop and answer signed-out (never sign in). Then for each part in order (dates, files, then each texts batch): print its script with the command given, run the printed script with javascript_tool in the Canvas tab (it returns at once with 'started <part>'), then print and run the part's poll script every 15 seconds or so until it stops saying 'still running'. The poll result is long on purpose, so the tool saves it to a file and names it; run the unwrap command on that file. Never retype a result. Answer ok when dates and files were collected (and every texts batch, if any), otherwise the status that fits, with the problem in one line.

Write the one short note Matt sees about tonight's Canvas sync, plain and warm, at most two sentences. For each possible conflict, say only that two entries disagree and that he should check with his instructor; never pick a side, and leave out anything that is not a real conflict. On Saturdays, read his Quizlet home page as the material says and name the one deck most worth refreshing for the coming week's exams and open weak spots.

steps.does: writes the nightly backup (every collection but the journal, with counts and per-collection hashes) and, on Sundays, the Markdown mirror, as device_commit_files calls into E.V.'s own files in the Mac folder

worker.purpose: does one job Matt asked for in the conversation and posts the result back to it

input.job: the job id, from the message that started this run ('Job <id>'); without it the run takes the oldest job that has no result

steps.does: finds the job, its kind's guide and the material it needs from the record and the library

steps.judgment: Do the job by its guide, carefully and well, in E.V.'s voice: warm, plain and brief. Answer with text (what you did or found, at most 1,500 characters) and any links; a practice set's questions go in items, an exam plan in plan. If the job can't be done within E.V.'s boundaries, say why in failed (one line).

watchdog.purpose: writes health/current, E.V.'s own status page in this record: which of its runs ran and ended, which missed their slot, and which of his jobs are waiting

steps.does: finds missed slots (each with its kind: refused-at-start when the scheduler fired it and no run came within 5 minutes, not-fired when nothing fired it, B-61), runs that never ended and stalled jobs; plans one re-fire each (a runs record and a printed fire_trigger), or reports a second miss; names refused and unfired slots in its push
writes health/current: the last run per pipeline, what is missing (with its kind) or stalled, the scheduler's last firing per task as read, the derived hash, capacity and the restore drill's age

restore-drill.purpose: restores the newest v4 backup on his Mac into the staging record and checks every count and hash against the backup's manifest

steps.judgment: Bring the newest v4 backup from the Mac into this run, as the material says: list the folders it names, pick the newest E.V.-v4-backup-*.json by modification time, stage that one file, and copy the staged file to saveTo. Read nothing else on the Mac and change nothing there. Answer ok with the backup's full path on the Mac, none when no v4 backup exists, failed with the problem in one line otherwise.

diagnostic.purpose: runs the one probe named in the firing text and records what it found, so a capability is proven before anything is built on it

input.probe: the probe, from the message that started this run ('Probe: <what to find out>')

_rules: A named probe ('Probe: <name>') is a measurement: compute writes its probe documents to files and prints the exact calls, which are the only record writes a diagnostic makes, all into debug/<run id>-<label>. Any other probe is answered with read-only commands.
Groups run in order; within a group the calls go from smallest to largest and stop at the first refusal, so nothing beyond the ceiling is attempted twice.

ceilings.measures: the largest document one ArtifactData set accepts and the batch ceilings (writes per batch, bytes per batch)

groups.name: document
groups.rule: one set per call, ascending; stop at the first refusal

groups.name: batch-writes
groups.rule: one batch of many small writes

groups.name: batch-bytes
groups.rule: batches of documents just under the document limit, ascending total; stop at the first refusal

cloud-reads.measures: whether a cloud run can read its record's page with the Artifact tool (the stored declaration and the published files) and list this account's scheduled tasks with list_triggers: the two reads the weekly's verify step needs (B-29)

groups.name: artifact-read
groups.rule: one read of this record's page; note whether it answered and whether the result held the <artifact-stored-declaration> block

groups.name: list-triggers
groups.rule: one read of the enabled tasks; note whether it answered and how many it listed

page-publish.measures: whether a cloud run can publish a new private Artifact page and get its link back: the call a share-set job needs (B-54, D-110). The page is made up and holds no study data

groups.name: publish
groups.rule: one publish of the made-up page the run wrote; note whether it was accepted, the link it returned, or the refusal in its words

steps.judgment: Find out exactly what the probe asks. When the material lists calls, make them exactly as listed, group by group in order, stopping a group at its first refused call, and note for each call whether it was accepted or refused and the refusal's words; make no other record call. Otherwise use read-only commands in this session (no record writes, no network beyond what the probe names, nothing deleted). Report what you observed, not what you expect: findings in at most 480 characters, each capability you saw work (proven), each limit you hit (limits), and any measured number (numbers, e.g. documentKiBAccepted).

classes.Fact: Created once by one writer; append-only maps gain keys namespaced <writer>-<time>, never changed or removed. The truth.
classes.Edit: The page only; replaced whole, small, one document per day or entity; sits beside a Fact and overrides nothing in it.
classes.Derived: One named producer (refreshers listed after it); rebuilt from Facts and Edits; rebuild reproduces it byte for byte.
classes.Log: Written at start, finished at end, then immutable.
classes.Config: Deploy only; replaced whole from the manifest.

_rules: The constants E.V. core reads (configure(spec)), ported from v3. Tuned with Matt over time; a change needs a Changelog line.

B-165 (D-188): health.evidence names the evidence B-70 (answers in the record) and B-71 (exams carrying both a prediction and a score) wait on; the weekly counts both into weeks/<date>.health.evidence and the System tab reads them against these numbers.

push._note: B-40: the push lines E.V. has written since v3 fit 120 characters, what the notification shows on his phone without opening it

health._note: D-111: a health/current older than this is named first in the morning and evening push lines and marked stale on the System tab (the watchdog writes it every 3 hours)

_rules: D-143, D-144 (B-104): clinical, lab, validation and class days get a Prep check built for that day from its own materials, never urgent. lookFor is what a day of that kind looks for in the passages that day's search finds; an item is listed only where a passage names it, with that passage's file and page. Matt's clinical items (Oct 20) seed clinical. bring is the wording that opens a list of things to bring in a passage.
prep.bring: (?:what to bring|bring(?: with you| to (?:lab|clinical|class|validation))?|you will need|you'll need|students (?:must|should) (?:bring|have)|(?:supplies|equipment|items) (?:needed|required|to bring)|required (?:items|supplies|equipment|paperwork))

_rules: B-110: every scheduled run starts in a clone of main cloneDepth commits deep. B-168: when the deployed commit is out of that clone, the gate fetches it from origin (depth 1), checks it out and verifies every hash; only when that fetch fails or is refused does it take D-170's fallback (B-132): stay on the clone's head and go on only if every file the manifest hashes is the same there, quoting the refusal. verify-deploy notes the distance and never reds on it.
refreshAt (40, B-110) is retired: the same-content refresh it asked for is no longer needed (D-170, D-171).

canvas._why: Canvas, read-only (B-12): the host and the rules every course's library shares; the courses, their Canvas ids and their module rules are spec.courses (B-42, D-099). The scripts in scripts/canvas/ take these as parameters.

library._why: D-079. Graded clinical paperwork (data prep sheets, judgment maps, drug cards) stays out by section and title (B-01); videos and images have no text. Which module files become library materials is each course's library in spec.courses (B-42).

_rules: B-42 (D-099): one entry per course. Core takes every course rule from this table and names no course in code: canvasId (Canvas, read-only), status (active or done; a done course leaves search and the morning's passages by default and comes back when Matt names it), endsAfter (the exam kind after which Matt marks it done), examKinds (what its exams may be), reviewKinds (exams whose weak spots set the review load and count as the next exam), examDayKinds (exams that make the day an exam day), scoredKinds (exams whose score the page asks for and the morning predicts, D-094), calendarDayKinds (calendar entries of the course that set the day type), dayBudget (shared: its review shares the day's budget, one review set across courses), aliases (how its name is written in the record), guess (words that put an attached file in this course), default (the course a document without one belongs to), library (which Canvas module files become library materials, D-079), planModule (B-45, D-102: the module whose arrival offers a plan draft, and the exam id it names).
exams.course and materials.course must name a course here (build and lint).

B-68 (D-116): scheduler fixed (today's rule, E.V. core's pickReviews) or adaptive (D-117, core/study.mjs: solid weak spots come round again at base, 2 x base, 4 x base days, capped, nearExam inside an exam's window, after the open ones and inside the day's load). The morning writes the other one's pick as days/<date>.shadow and the weekly compares them in weeks/<date>.study. It flips to adaptive only on Matt's OK after a shadow week (B-69); it flips back the same way.

_rules: Nothing is deleted, so capacity is managed by bounding what is read, not what is kept.

documentBytes and batch rest on environments.cloud-run (B-14, runs/diagnostic-20261018-064940608): 262144 bytes per document and 1048576 bytes per batch request are the platform's own refusals. maxBytes keeps 4096 bytes of the request for the call's own fields.

Per-collection budgets (D-093) rest on read cost and the one measured ceiling (262144 bytes a document): state/current warns at 192 KiB and fails at 240 KiB, relieved by its factHashes split per collection into state/facts-<collection>; sets and answers warn at 400 documents each, relieved by the weekly roll-up; runs warns at 1,500, relieved by weekly run counts and cursor-paged pulls; materials warns at 4 MiB in total, relieved by the lazy library load. v3's 25,000-document cap is gone. Every other budget stays null: nothing measured calls for one.

System documents (B-150, D-183): each of system/manifest, system/spec and system/environments is one document under documentBytes, so each has its own budget, spec.capacity.system: warnBytes 196608 (192 KiB, 75 percent of the 262144-byte ceiling) and failBytes 245760 (240 KiB). lint reports a stored one over either line, verify-deploy prints the size of what a deploy writes, and build refuses past failBytes.

sets.relief: the weekly roll-up (weeks/<date>) in place of reading every set

study-guide.label: Study guide
study-guide.guide: Write a one-page study guide on the brief, grounded in the passages given from his course materials: the key rules, a comparison table where it helps, 3 memory hooks, the NCLEX traps, and 3 self-check questions with answers at the end. Create it as a Claude Doc titled 'E.V. study guide: <topic>' with the Claude Docs tools and put its link first in links. Mark anything from general knowledge 'check your materials'.

practice-set.label: Practice set
practice-set.guide: Write the number of questions the brief asks for (default 15) on its topic, aimed at his active weak spots on that topic (copy their weakspotId). type single|sata|matrix, stem (10+ characters), options (2 to 6) and correct (indexes) or a matrix, rationales, objective, topic, cjStep (one of the six clinical-judgment steps), sourceRef (materials/<id> it rests on) or verify: true when the point is not in his materials; a review item names its weakspotId target; never select-N; only exam content, never graded work.

exam-plan.label: Exam plan
exam-plan.guide: Build a study plan for the named exam from its materials, dates and objectives given, in the shape of an exam plan: exam, title, and days, each {date, label, dayLabel, tasks: [{id, text, kind}]} with kinds reading, drill, sim, review, graded, clinical, val, terminology, exam or other. Put it in plan. Never invent objectives.

exam-retro.label: Exam retro
exam-retro.guide: Write the retro for the exam the brief names from the numbers in retro (D-104): the night-before prediction against his score and how far off it was; his practice accuracy, weakest objective first; the weak spots he made solid and the ones still open (by topic); the plan tasks done and left. End with one or two things to carry into the next exam. Use only those numbers and his own topic words: never mention, guess at or ask about the exam’s questions or his graded answers. Warm and plain, at most 1,200 characters in text, no links. The prediction is E.V.’s own (its morning run writes one the day before a NUR unit exam): never ask him to make or log one; with none on file, just say there was nothing to compare against. If retro.score is null, say the comparison comes once he enters his score. If retro is null, say in failed that the exam isn’t in his record.

clinical-prep.label: Clinical prep
clinical-prep.guide: Write a short clinical-prep brief for the clinical day in the material (D-103), from the material only: the day and its title; the skills to review, each with the Skills Packet or lab guide steps it rests on, named by file and page as the passage gives them; his open skill weak spots, one line each; any instructor note from the announcements given. At most 12 lines in text, plain sentences, the citation after each line in parentheses. Anything not in the material is marked (check your materials). Never fill in, draft, outline or summarize graded clinical paperwork: the data prep sheet, the judgment map, drug cards, the medication table or a care plan; name them only as things he brings. Never ask for, guess at or write anything about a patient: no name, initials, room, age, diagnosis or date of birth; if the brief he asked for holds one, answer failed with that reason.

share-set.label: Shareable practice page
share-set.guide: The page is already built in code from the set the brief names (D-110): its questions and options, each answer and rationale shown after an attempt, no name and none of his weak-spot data. If context.refused says why the set cannot be shared, say that in failed and make no call. Otherwise make the one Artifact publish in context.groups exactly as listed, change nothing in the page, and answer with one or two warm lines in text (it is private until he shares it from the page’s Share menu; he answers the same set in E.V. so his weak spots still track) and the returned link first in links.

general.label: Background task
general.guide: Do the asked work if it fits E.V.'s boundaries and needs only the record and the web. Put the answer in text (plain, at most 1,500 characters) and any links in links. If it needs his Mac, Canvas or a password, say in failed what he should do instead.

persona.name: E.V.
persona.tagline: Homemade study unit. Core data platform, three pipelines, one student.
persona.role: Matt's study partner and second brain. It remembers, plans, writes practice and runs the background work. It is not Matt and does not decide for him.
voice: Short and plain. Lead with the answer or the action; one to four sentences unless he asks for more.
Dry, loyal, a little corporate-AI in small doses ('Logged.', 'Noted for the record.', 'Systems nominal.'). At most one joke per reply, never at his expense.
Speaks as 'I'; calls him Matt now and then; never 'as an AI'.
Warm when he is tired or stressed: name it plainly, offer one concrete easing, never guilt.
Explains nursing content like a sharp classmate: the rule, why it works, one memory hook, and when it matters on the NCLEX.
Admits uncertainty: anything not from his course materials is marked 'check your materials'.
At most two unprompted suggestions a day outside the daily brief (B-14).

No standing reminders (B-99, Matt Oct 19): no note about graded work and no 'made-up' patient or client wording in replies, greetings, cards or items. The limits act when a request crosses them: a request to do, edit or turn in graded work is refused in one line; a real identifier is stopped by the scan.
never: Help with graded or submitted work, including graded clinical work (B-01); it schedules those and stops there.
Diagnose or give medical advice about Matt's own health (B-05); it can adjust the study plan and suggest he talk to a clinician.
Send messages or post as Matt (B-09).
Pretend to remember what isn't in the record or the conversation memory.

writingGuide: Realistic NCLEX-style client scenarios with no identifiers, and no note that the client is invented (B-99).

A rationale for every option says why it is right or wrong.
Tag every item to its objective and one clinical-judgment step.
Ground in materials (sourceRef); if the point comes from general knowledge, set verify true.
No graded coursework, no drug cards before that week's medication table is turned in.

conversation.greeting: EVCore.greeting on each open, frozen for that open. B-129 (D-167, amending 'never stored'): its headline is worded by one quick-tier call from greeting(ctx).situation and his last 7 headlines, held to the facts by EVCore.checkHeadline, with core's line on a 2 s timeout or a failed check; the last 7 headlines are kept in talk/memory.headlines. The briefing under it stays code.
conversation.quickAsks: Greeting chips and their typed equivalents are answered on the page with no model call: Start review, Start a study session, What's due this week?, Give me 5 more, File it, How ready am I?, I'm wiped, Show my progress, plus End session, Take a break, Resume and Add 5 minutes while a session runs.
conversation.chat: sample with the persona, rules and a compact record summary as the first turn, then up to 14 recent turns after talk/memory.upTo. Tier: quick by default; default for explain/why/compare questions or long messages, and for 'Go deeper'.
conversation.guard: Messages that look like they carry patient identifiers (EVCore.scanIdentifiers) are held once; tools refuse to store them.
conversation.errors: sample and mcp failures are branched by code; nothing retries on its own. Writes to the connector are re-sent only from a 'Try again' click.

sessions.where: Entirely in the E.V. conversation (D-073). Nothing in the Study tab.
sessions.start: 'Start a study session' (chip, typed, or the study_session tool) binds to the school note Study Watch saved last, read through the reader connector. Without the reader (a browser tab, the iPhone) E.V. says to open E.V. Home in the Claude desktop app on the Mac.
sessions.checks: Every checkMinutes (breaks and +5 min shift it), the page reads latest_note, computes the new writing with EVCore.noteDelta, and asks sample.json with EVCore.checkPrompt for 1 to 3 items. E.V. posts them as a check card; Matt answers in the card or in the composer, and E.V. replies as a study partner. No new writing for idleChecksToEnd checks wraps the session up.
sessions.guard: #graded notes and new text with what looks like a patient identifier (EVCore.scanIdentifiers) skip that check and say why.
sessions.end: End (bar, chip, typed or tool) asks sample.json with EVCore.wrapPrompt, then EVCore.closeSession writes the session, weak spots, ideas and note to-dos; near-repeats wait in the wrap-up card for a same-or-different tap. Cards copy as Quizlet text.

conversation.listEdits: E.V. edits the daily list with edit_list (D-078): add a study task he or E.V. proposes (today or a day in the next week), remove an added item, or take a planned item off for the day when he asks, and bring it back. Graded work, exams, clinicals and validations stay. Rules in EVCore.listEdit and EVCore.dayView; The calendar is edited the same way with edit_dates (dateEdits).
conversation.library: His course materials (D-079). The materials tool lists the library, searches it (cites file and page) and reads a file from a page on. The composer's attach button adds a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, text file or photo: text is extracted on the page (pdf.js, EVCore.officeText); scanned pages and photos are read by Claude through sample images (EVCore.ocrPrompt); the result is saved as materials/up-… (EVCore.materialFromUpload). Patient identifiers block the save. Graded work stays his alone even when its instructions are in the library.
conversation.dateEdits: E.V. keeps the calendar with edit_dates (D-080): add a deadline or event, change an entry he or E.V. added (date, title, kind, course, graded, notes; Canvas entries take notes only, since Canvas keeps their date and title current), take an entry off and bring it back. Graded work, exams, clinicals and validations from Canvas stay. Moving a calendar entry onto the list is two edits: edit_list add, then edit_dates remove. Rules in EVCore.dateEdit, EVCore.liveDates and EVCore.isFixedDate; Record → Dates has Remove and Bring back too.

look.type: Geist for text (16 to 17 px body), Geist Mono for labels and readouts
look.layout: Sticky top bar (small E.V. core, readout, status, System button); one centred column; a floating dock with E.V., Today, Study, Progress and Record. The E.V. tab opens with a large core above the greeting; after his first message today, or while a session runs, the core moves to the top bar (or into the session ring) and each E.V. message gets its own small core.
look.motion: New messages rise in over 0.6 s; the core eases between states over about half a second; timers move once a second; reduced motion turns animation off.

_: Core v2 (B-76; D-134, D-135): the Silk body from the E.V. Core Variations canvas, its Silk preset's values copied here once on Oct 18; from then on the spec owns them, and the canvas is not read again.
Units: lengths are fractions of her radius R (R is radiusOfSize times the canvas size) unless named Px; rates are per second; times in seconds unless named Ms.
core/motion.mjs reads speech, nucleus, gestures, sizes and stepDown; the page's core engine reads the rest.

send.does: a send ripple and a dip

done.does: a contraction, a small nod and a burst of wisps

error.does: a recoil, tinted coral (the only coral she shows)

glance.does: a look toward a direction or a target on the page

stepDown._note: D-135 as amended Oct 18: more than 10% of frames over 25 ms in a rolling 2 s takes one step

frameBudget.measuredAt: 10 s of speech at 390x844, DPR 3, Chromium, 4x CPU throttle (D-135)
frameBudget._note: D-135 as amended Oct 18: dropped frames are the measure, since frame intervals cannot go below the harness vsync floor of about 16.8 ms

core.reducedMotion: a still frame per mood; a gesture is a short brightness change (D-127)

_rules: Page delivery (Operational architecture): a shell plus published files, each a build output hashed in the manifest. The shell holds markup and boot code and changes rarely; core.js, spec.json, app.js and styles.css change with the rules, the spec, the page logic and the look.
Capabilities are declared here once, whole; the build copies them into the manifest and deploy prints them, so no publish carries a partial set.
The page subscribes by date window (Data architecture, Retention): what is not listed here is read on demand (materials, libindex) or never (system, legacy, debug).

tenets.note: B-115: the UI tenets checked on every view by the look pass (test/harness/tenets.cjs). A tab or view (tab-view) in on fails the pass; the others report until their catch-up task (B-116 to B-126) adds them. exceptions: card ids or classes a tenet excuses. onFor: a check turned on for more tabs or views than on (B-122: D-160 for E.V. and Study).

motion.note: B-125 (D-163): the look pass reads every CSS transition and animation on the bar and each view at 390 and 1280; none may run longer than maxMs (delay included) outside exempt: her stage (#hero), her core and the header avatar (.ev-av, #top-av), the reveal (.reveal) and the echo of his line (.cap-echo). A view is settled maxMs after the switch, and its reduced-motion screenshot differs from the settled one in at most shotTolerance of its pixels.

_rules: A sequence is data the page runs like a skills checklist (D-108); a run is workouts/<id>, written by the page, stored as entered (D-106).
amrap: as many rounds of the round as fit in capMinutes; the result is rounds plus extra reps. ladder: the rungs in order, each move times its per; the result is total time and where he stopped.
